clue.text: Disease picked up when the impossible happened

indicators.note: picked up as in heard, so the phrase is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: 'when pigs fly' stands for the impossible, so the impossible happening is swine flew

explanation.surface: An illness caught at some miraculous moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When pigs fly' is the idiom for something that will never happen, so the impossible happening is SWINE FLEW, which sounds like SWINE FLU.
explanation.definitionFit: Swine flu is an influenza strain, a named illness that spread widely in 2009.

clue.text: Found out concealing key to correcting erroneous input

indicators.note: the words found out are said to conceal the answer, which sits inside them across the word break

explanation.surface: A discovery that hides the right key for fixing a typing mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' marks the letters hidden in foUND Out.
explanation.definitionFit: Software has an undo command, often a dedicated key, for reversing a mistaken keystroke.

clue.text: Core position of hospital in NHS

definitions.meaning: H, the abbreviation for hospital, is the central letter of NHS, the UK's National Health Service

explanation.surface: Hospitals are central to Britain's health service.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service; H for hospital is its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A core is the central part of something, its centre or heart.

clue.text: Champion finds partner online?

parts.note: E as in e-mail is the prefix for anything online
a spouse is a marriage partner

explanation.surface: Someone finds a mate through internet dating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' is a verb here, not a winner.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to support or advocate it, as a champion does.

clue.text: US stock market regulator head promoted under European principles

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means the following letters sit below the abbreviation for European
in a down clue, promoted means sent upward, so the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: the SEC is the Securities and Exchange Commission, which regulates American markets
a ness is a headland, a geographical head

explanation.surface: An American regulator's chief is raised to a post beneath a European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' turns SEC + NESS upward to SSENCES, and 'under' places it below E. 'head' is a headland (NESS), not a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: The essences of a matter are its fundamental elements, its core principles.

clue.text: Unexpected visitor in winter trying to sell you something?

definitions.text: Unexpected visitor in winter trying to sell you something?

parts.words: Unexpected visitor in winter trying to sell you something?
parts.note: a caller arriving in chilly weather, and also a salesperson phoning or knocking without an appointment

explanation.surface: A winter doorstep salesman nobody expected.
explanation.walkthrough: A salesperson who rings or knocks unannounced is the stock phrase; winter adds the literal chill.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold caller makes unsolicited sales approaches to people with no prior contact.

clue.text: Resolution satisfied ownership of property after it is abandoned

parts.note: to have met a need is to have satisfied it

indicators.note: abandoned means dropped, so those two letters leave the word for ownership

parts.note: title is legal ownership of property

explanation.surface: A legal matter of satisfying an ownership claim on derelict property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is abandoned' removes IT from TITLE, leaving TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mettle is courage and determination, a synonym of resolution in the sense of resolve.

clue.text: They roared with wind by two but were swinging by three!

definitions.text: They roared with wind by two but were swinging by three!

parts.words: They roared with wind by two but were swinging by three!
parts.note: doubled they are the Roaring Forties winds, tripled the Swinging Sixties

explanation.surface: Something that roared, then blew a gale, then swung.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1920s are the Roaring Twenties; multiply by two for the Roaring Forties, strong westerly winds of the Southern Ocean, and by three for the Swinging Sixties.
explanation.definitionFit: The decade of the 1920s, known for jazz and exuberance, is nicknamed the Roaring Twenties.

clue.text: Bathroom fitting is more splashy when I get in

indicators.note: when introduces the condition that turns the answer into the word for more splashy
if the letter gets in, the answer becomes the longer word; so it is taken out here

parts.note: showier means more flashy or splashy

explanation.surface: A bathroom shower looks flashier once someone climbs in.
explanation.walkthrough: Backwards wordplay: 'when I get in' says the answer with I inserted becomes SHOWIER, so take I out of SHOWIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A shower is a standard fixture in a bathroom, a fitting plumbed in.

clue.text: Apprentice never tried out leads for setter

indicators.note: the leads of the words are their front letters, taken in turn

explanation.surface: A beginner who has never tried something, giving pointers to a setter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads' takes the first letters of Apprentice never tried out.
explanation.definitionFit: Anto is the pseudonym of this puzzle's compiler, so the name stands for the setter.

clue.text: Obey Lorna, perhaps, by revising study …

parts.note: Lorna Doone is the heroine of R. D. Blackmore's novel, so her surname is a plausible example

indicators.note: revising means reworking, so the letters of study are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tells Lorna to do what she is told and revise.
explanation.walkthrough: Lorna Doone is the title heroine of R. D. Blackmore's 1869 novel set on Exmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: To do one's duty is to carry out what is required, much as obeying does.

clue.text: … recently put back in metal folder

indicators.note: put back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words metal folder

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something was lately returned to a steel filing folder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the hidden run ETALFO in mETAL FOlder; 'put back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Of late is an idiom meaning lately, in the recent past.

clue.text: Unreal chef cooked something that's supposedly never available

indicators.note: cooked as in cooked up or doctored, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fantasy chef prepared the meal nobody can get.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges UNREAL CHEF.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'there's no such thing as a free lunch' means nothing comes without some cost.

clue.text: Philosopher abandoning case makes a cry for help

definitions.meaning: the classical Athenian thinker, teacher of Plato

definitions.text: abandoning case makes a cry for help
definitions.meaning: a word that, once a crate (case) is taken out of it, leaves SOS, the distress call

explanation.surface: A thinker drops his court case and calls for help.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half works backwards: take CRATE, a packing case, out of the answer and the distress call SOS is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates was the classical Athenian thinker whose questioning method Plato recorded.

clue.text: Foremost Irish girl gets discharge, when rejected

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Emer is an Irish girl's name, from the legendary wife of Cu Chulainn
pus is discharge from a wound

explanation.surface: A leading Irish woman suffers an infection after being turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when rejected' reverses EMERPUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means highest in rank, the foremost or greatest of all.

clue.text: Modest men daily get abused

indicators.note: abused means mistreated or knocked about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unassuming men are mistreated every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get abused' rearranges MEN DAILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidenly means shy and demure like a young girl, hence modest in manner.

clue.text: Impractical for campuses to become temporary shelters?

definitions.meaning: of no practical value or purpose

definitions.text: for campuses to become temporary shelters?
definitions.meaning: read as an instruction: take use out of campuses and camps, temporary shelters, remain

explanation.surface: Universities being turned into emergency housing would be no good.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half works backwards: split the answer as USE-LESS, an instruction to drop USE, and CAMPUSES becomes CAMPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something useless serves no purpose, so it is of no practical value.

clue.text: Broke unit revealing shade on the outside

parts.note: skint is British slang for having no money
one is the unit number

explanation.surface: A financially ruined business unit shows its shadowy exterior.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is everyday British slang for penniless. 'shade on the outside' is the colour of the skin, the body's outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin tone is a shade of complexion, the colour shown on the body's surface.

clue.text: Almost miss promotion that could help ascending the slippery slope

definitions.text: that could help ascending the slippery slope

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to skip something is to miss it out
a lift is a boost or rise, a promotion

explanation.surface: Narrowly missing out on a career step on the way up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops P from SKIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski lift carries skiers up a snowy mountain, which the slippery slope playfully describes.

clue.text: A Swedish group has poetic scheme for this Lear favourite

definitions.text: A Swedish group has poetic scheme for this Lear favourite

parts.words: A Swedish group has poetic scheme for this Lear favourite
parts.note: A plus ABBA, the Swedish pop group, gives AABBA, the rhyme pattern of the verse form Edward Lear popularised

explanation.surface: A Swedish band's song structure is linked to a nonsense poet's favourite form.
explanation.walkthrough: The verse form rhymes AABBA, which is A + ABBA; Edward Lear wrote many in his Book of Nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Five-line comic verses rhyming AABBA are the form Edward Lear made famous.

clue.text: Cast-iron commercial progress

indicators.note: cast as in thrown or moulded anew, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: Ironworks advertising its growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' rearranges IRON to INRO.
explanation.definitionFit: To make an inroad is to make progress into something, an advance.

clue.text: Aristocrat without a scrap found outside city

indicators.note: the word for scrap is found on the outside, wrapping round the rest

parts.note: to bin something is to scrap it

indicators.note: without means lacking, so that letter is removed from the nobleman

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A penniless nobleman discovered outside a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops A from the nobleman, leaving ERL; 'found outside' wraps the scrap word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Berlin is the capital city of Germany.

clue.text: He holds the money when company meets in bar

indicators.note: in places the meeting inside the word for bar

parts.note: to bar is to ban
an AGM is a company's annual general meeting

explanation.surface: The treasurer sits in the pub while the firm gathers.
explanation.walkthrough: A company meets at its AGM, annual general meeting; 'in' puts it inside the word for bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagman collects or carries money, often illicit cash for a racket.

clue.text: Masons may roll it up to reveal support

definitions.text: Masons may roll it up to reveal support

parts.words: Masons may roll it up to reveal support
parts.note: Doing so reveals a leg, which supports the body

explanation.surface: Builders roll something up to expose a structural support.
explanation.walkthrough: In Freemasons' initiation rites a candidate rolls up a trouser leg; the bared leg is the 'support'.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of trousers covering one leg is what Freemasons famously roll up in ritual.

clue.text: It comes early for one being sent off

definitions.text: It comes early for one being sent off

parts.words: It comes early for one being sent off
parts.note: sports slang: a player dismissed before the final whistle heads for the changing room's tub ahead of team-mates

explanation.surface: Something arrives early for a departing person.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'early bath' is British sports slang for a player sent off the field before the end of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Players bathe after a game, so a dismissed player gets to the bath before the rest.

clue.text: Time attempt to capture rook

indicators.note: capture means hold inside, so the chess piece goes within the word for attempt

parts.note: a bid is an attempt
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess player's moment to try taking a rook.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRD is British slang for a prison sentence, time inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing bird means serving time in prison, so bird is a slang synonym for a sentence.

clue.text: Standard element of animation plot

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
a cel is a single painted frame in traditional cartoon animation

explanation.surface: A routine piece of a cartoon's storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' is a piece of land, not a storyline.
explanation.definitionFit: A parcel of land is a plot, a defined area of ground.

clue.text: After signal, shout 'open'

indicators.note: after places the word for shout following the word for signal

parts.note: to flag is to signal
to rant is to shout angrily

explanation.surface: Following a signal, someone yells to open up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open' means blatant here, not unlocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant means conspicuously obvious, done openly and shamelessly.
